key_points.point: The document highlights that AI is already driving significant productivity gains across diverse sectors, including finance, insurance, and retail. By automating repetitive tasks and assisting with complex queries, AI allows employees to focus on higher-value work. This aligns with the accelerationist view that AI is a tool for immediate societal progress and efficiency.
key_points.verbatim: “We have AI-enabled productivity tools that are used by more than 60,000 associates to help reduce repetitive tasks, so teams can focus more on supporting our members and providers,” says Boudreaux.

key_points.point: The document argues that the best way to understand AI's potential is through real-world deployment and adoption. By observing how companies integrate AI into their operations, we can learn how to improve these tools. This practical, iterative approach is central to the accelerationist belief in learning by doing.
key_points.verbatim: “What you’re seeing is that the women-CEO-led companies are showing up to adopt new technologies, in some ways that are consistent to some of the consumer adoption behavior we’ve seen in other technologies,” says Lareina Yee, McKinsey Global Institute director and a senior partner at the consultancy.

key_points.point: The document acknowledges that past technological trends, such as social media, were developed without sufficient foresight regarding their long-term societal harms. It suggests that AI presents a critical opportunity to avoid repeating these mistakes by proactively asking how to bring AI into the workforce responsibly. This reflects a safetyist concern for preventing dystopian outcomes through early intervention.
key_points.verbatim: “I think it’s an incredible opportunity for women to ask the right questions of, how should we responsibly bring AI into the workforce and into our homes and into our lives?” asks Franklin. “We don’t want to end up with a bad, dystopian outcome.”

key_points.point: The document notes that while AI is being adopted, there is a significant focus on productivity and automation, which can lead to the displacement of repetitive tasks. Skeptics would argue that this necessitates proactive management to ensure workers are not left behind. The focus on retraining employees is a key mechanism for managing this transition.
key_points.verbatim: Financial giant Citigroup’s (No. 38) recent AI efforts have included retraining 175,000 employees on how to write better prompts to generate more impactful results from large language model queries.

key_points.point: The document acknowledges that past technologies like social media were developed by men without sufficient consideration for their harmful impacts on users. This supports the skeptic's argument that we must be critical of who builds technology and how it is deployed, rather than assuming it will naturally benefit everyone.
key_points.verbatim: Social media is a form of technology that was mostly built by men, and it wasn’t until years later that studies began to reveal how harmful it could be to users, including mothers and teenage girls.

factual_claims.claim: Women lead 18% of the companies on the Fortune AIQ 50 list, compared to 11% of all Fortune 500 companies in 2025.
Citigroup retrained 175,000 employees on prompt engineering for large language models.
Women make up 29% of C-suite positions as of 2024, up from 17% in 2015.
